title: A Message From the Boss
story: The message from the boss arrives while the Technician is still at his console. YOKE mentions it like an afterthought. The screen opens on a nose: the boss is far too close to the camera. He backs off, turns a circle on his chair the way dogs do, and sits. He is Supervisor Barnabas of the Clearance Office, Sector Nine, a golden retriever in the Empire's black jacket, and he has read the first field report, the whole thing, twice; it is on his desk with tooth marks in one corner. He says his piece about honest work as solemnly as a dog holding a stay. Then a ball rolls across the back of his office and he is gone, all of him, for the length of one panel. He comes back sheepish and says the kindest thing in the message. By the time he gets to how much he loves reports his tail has cleared the desk. He signs off with 'Good boy', and ends the call with his nose. YOKE, who adores him, has the last word. Every spoken line is the game's own (content/boss.ts); the only new words are sounds.
content: Science-fiction satire for adults, work-safe: no nudity, no sex, no gore.

style.look: A cinematic photoreal frame of hard science fiction in an ascetic far-future empire: matte black and bare pale ceramic surfaces, flush seams, even white strip light, razor-thin holographic displays, extreme plainness, no ornament, no neon, no clutter. The only marking anywhere is one small plain black gear symbol. Candid and natural, like a frame caught from life, never posed for a portrait.

cast.name: YOKE
cast.description: the ship's AI. She is a HOLOGRAM and the only drawn thing in a photoreal room: a waist-up projection rendered as a flat-colour anime illustration with crisp linework, glowing pale blue, slightly translucent, with faint scan lines. An adult woman of about twenty-four with a calm, intelligent face, long straight pale silver hair with a faint blue tint falling well past her shoulders, a side-swept fringe, amber-gold eyes, fair skin, one small plain black gear-shaped hair clip, a plain black high-collared long-sleeved dress with a narrow white inner collar

cast.name: the Technician
cast.description: a slight young man of about twenty-five, photoreal, always seen from behind: untidy dark hair, a stylus tucked behind his right ear, a plain black high-collared uniform with a narrow white collar, the sleeves pushed up to the elbows. His face is never shown

cast.name: Supervisor Barnabas
cast.description: an uplifted dog who is a supervisor in the empire's bureaucracy. He is a real golden retriever in every way: a dog's body, a dog's legs and paws, a dog's posture and movement, a feathered tail; never a human body, never human shoulders, arms or hands. He wears a plain black high-collared uniform jacket tailored for a dog: it covers his chest, shoulders and front legs down to the wrists and has a narrow white inner collar; his back half and tail are bare golden fur. A kind, eager, trusting face
cast.sheet: A lifelike photograph. Supervisor Barnabas, an uplifted dog who is a bureaucrat of an ascetic far-future empire, in a plain pale ceramic office with flush seams and even white light. He is a real golden retriever in every way, with a dog's body, legs, paws and feathered tail, sitting on a grey office chair the way a dog sits: haunches down on the seat, front legs straight, front paws resting on the edge of a bare pale desk. He wears a plain black high-collared uniform jacket tailored for a dog's body: it covers his chest, shoulders and front legs down to the wrists, with a narrow white inner collar; his back half and tail are bare golden fur. No human body, no human shoulders, no human arms or hands. Seen from the front and a little to one side so the whole dog is visible from ears to tail, ears up, mouth a little open in a happy pant, bright kind eyes. One dog only. No badge, no medal, no insignia.

panels.picture: The ship's operations room. YOKE's hologram stands on the black console, waist up, one hand lifted in an offhand 'by the way' gesture, a small amused smile. The Technician stands at the console at the left edge of the frame, seen from behind. The upper left of the frame is plain dark wall.

words.text: Oh, and we got a message from the boss.

panels.picture: The ship's operations room: a large flat glowing display floats above the black console and fills most of the frame. On the display, the video feed: an enormous, slightly out-of-focus wet black dog nose and one warm brown eye, far too close to the camera. At the bottom left of the frame, small and dark, the back of the Technician's head, leaning back a little in surprise. The only dog is the one on the display: there is no dog in the room, and nobody else in the room.
panels.camera: from behind the Technician, the display large in frame

panels.picture: The video feed, full frame: a plain pale ceramic office, a bare pale desk, one grey office chair. Supervisor Barnabas has backed away from the camera and is turning a circle on the seat of the chair before sitting, the way dogs do: caught mid-turn, side-on to us, all four paws on the seat, tail up, looking over his shoulder at the camera.

The video feed: Supervisor Barnabas now sits on the chair as a dog sits, haunches down, front paws up on the edge of the bare desk, ears up, mouth open in a happy pant, looking straight into the camera. The upper right of the frame is bare pale wall.
panels.camera: medium, at the dog's eye level

words.text: Technician! Supervisor Barnabas here, Clearance Office, Sector Nine.

panels.picture: The video feed, closer: on the bare desk lies a thin grey report tablet with clear tooth marks in one corner. Supervisor Barnabas holds it down with one front paw and nudges it toward the camera with his nose, eyes rolled up to the lens, bright and proud.

words.text: I just read your first field report, and I want you to know I read the whole thing. Twice!

panels.picture: The video feed: Supervisor Barnabas sits very straight and perfectly still on his chair, chin up, ears forward, solemn and proud, the way a dog holds a 'stay'. The right third of the frame is bare pale wall.

words.text: Pest clearance is honest work, and honest work is the best work there is.

panels.picture: The video feed: something has caught his attention. Supervisor Barnabas's whole head has snapped to one side, ears pricked, body rigid, one front paw lifted off the desk, staring at a small plain grey ball rolling slowly across the floor at the back of the office. His mouth is closed. He has completely forgotten the camera.
panels.camera: medium wide, the ball small in the background

panels.picture: The same office, the same chair and desk, a moment later: Supervisor Barnabas has turned back to the camera from his chair behind the desk, a little sheepish, ears back, head tilted to one side, looking up at the lens from under his brows, front paws on the desk. The left third of the frame is bare pale wall.

words.text: The Board says only the numbers matter, and the Board is very wise.
But I say you are a good egg.

panels.picture: The video feed, wider: Supervisor Barnabas is up on his feet on the chair with excitement, front paws planted on the desk, mouth open in a wide dog grin. His tail is a golden blur behind him and has just swept a cup of styluses off the end of the desk: the cup and the styluses are in mid-air.

words.text: Keep it up! I will be watching every report. I love reports.

panels.picture: The ship's operations room, over the Technician's shoulder: a large flat glowing display floats above the black console, showing the video feed. On the feed Supervisor Barnabas leans right into the camera, tongue out, eyes squeezed half shut with joy, his face filling most of the display. The Technician, seen from behind at the left edge of the frame, stands a little straighter than before. The only dog is the one on the display: there is no dog in the room.
panels.camera: over his shoulder, the display large in frame

words.text: Good boy. Good work! Good work.

panels.picture: The video feed, full frame: Supervisor Barnabas is ending the call with his nose. The frame is filled again by the big wet black nose pressing against the lens, slightly squashed, one eye crossed with concentration above it.
panels.camera: extreme close, the nose on the lens

panels.picture: The ship's operations room again, the display gone dark. YOKE's hologram on the console turns to the Technician with a wry, fond half-smile, one eyebrow up, a hand on her hip. The Technician, seen from behind at the left edge of the frame, has not moved.

words.text: A dog for a boss. Lucky you, honestly, they're lovely.
Just don't let him anywhere near the budget.
